EngLawName: Regulations Governing the Organization and Operation of the National Health Insurance Data Advisory Council
LawName: 全民健康保險資料諮議會組織及運作辦法
EngLawHistories: 1.Promulgated on August 7,2026, in accordance with the Ministry of Health and Welfare Order Wei-Pu-Pao-Tzu No. 1151260394. Promulgation shall take effect on August 10, 2026.

EngLawArticles.EngArticleContent: Regulations Governing the Organization and Operation of the National Health Insurance Data Advisory Council (hereinafter referred to as the “Regulations”) are promulgated pursuant to the provisions of Paragraph 3 of Article 5 of the National Health Insurance Data Management Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”).

Pursuant to Article 4 of the Act, the National Health Insurance Data Advisory Council (hereinafter referred to as the “Council”) shall perform the following duties:
1. To provide recommendations on policies, regulations, and supervision concerning the management and oversight of the use of National Health Insurance data (hereinafter referred to as “NHI data”) for purposes other than the specific purposes.
2. To provide consultations and conduct assessments regarding supervisory and protective measures for safeguarding the use of NHI data for purposes other than the specific purposes.
3. To handle disputes arising from applications for the use of NHI data for purposes other than the specific purposes.
4. To handle disputes concerning requests by data subjects to cease the use or provision of NHI data for purposes other than the specific purposes.
5. To assist the competent authority in guidance, evaluation, and supervision regarding entrusted management of the use of NHI data for purposes other than the specific purposes.
6. To provide recommendations on other matters related to NHI data.

The Council shall consist of twenty-one to twenty-seven members, one of whom shall serve as the convener. The head of the competent authority or a deputy minister designated by that head shall serve concurrently as convener. The remaining members shall be appointed or designated to serve concurrently as Council members from among the following persons, none of whom shall hold office as an elected representative:
1. Experts or scholars in the fields of medical care, public health, law, and cybersecurity, with at least two members from each field.
2. Representatives of human rights organizations and patient groups, and public figures who are considered fair and just, with at least two members from each category.
3. Representatives of government agencies/institutions, including at least one representative each from the Ministry of Digital Affairs, the National Science and Technology Council, and the competent authority and its subordinate agencies/institutions.
The combined number of members referred to in Subparagraphs 1 and 2 of the preceding paragraph shall constitute at least three-fourths of the total Council membership. Members of either gender shall constitute at least one-third of the total Council membership.

Council members shall serve a term of two years and may be reappointed or redesignated upon expiration of their terms.
A Council member shall be removed from office or shall not be reappointed or redesignated where, during the member’s term, the member resigns; changes the position by virtue of which the member represents a government agency, institution, or organization; becomes unable to perform the duties of office; assumes office as an elected representative; breaches the duties of office; or is otherwise seriously unfit to serve.
Where a vacancy arises during a member’s term of office for any reason or a member is removed from office, a replacement member may be appointed/designated. The replacement member shall serve for the remainder of the original member’s term.

The Council shall convene a meeting once every six months. Where necessary, extraordinary meetings may be convened.
Council meetings shall be chaired by the convener. Where the convener is unable to attend for any reason, the competent authority shall designate one member to serve as acting chair.
A meeting may be held only if more than half of all Council members are present. A resolution shall require the consent of more than half of the members present. In the event of a tie, the chair shall decide the matter.
Members shall attend Council meetings in person and may not appoint another person to attend on their behalf. However, this restriction does not apply to members serving as representatives of government agencies/institutions.
Authorized representatives under the proviso to the preceding paragraph shall be counted toward the number of attendees and may participate in discussions and vote at the meeting.
When conducting consultations or handling disputes, the Council may, as necessary, invite relevant experts, scholars, representatives of government agencies, institutions, legal persons, or organizations, and personnel relevant units of the competent authority and its subordinate agencies or institutions, to attend meetings in a nonmember capacity or provide written opinions.

Council members and other persons attending meetings shall maintain the confidentiality of meeting-related documents, data, and information that come to their knowledge or into their possession and shall not disclose them without justification.
Preparatory work for the Council’s consultations or dispute handling , its deliberative processes, the names of Council members and participating experts and scholars, and documents and data relating to deliberations shall be subject to restrictions on disclosure or withheld from provision in accordance with Article 18 of The Freedom of Government Information Law.
Matters concerning the recusal of Council members are governed by the Administrative Procedure Act.
These Regulations shall take effect on August 10, 2026.
